deck.title: Well-Architected Framework
deck.analogy: The Well-Architected Framework is a building inspector's checklist: a house can stand up and still fail inspection, and the six pillars are the six things the inspector checks.

subtopics.title: The exam angle (this is the real payoff)

cards.front: What is the AWS Well-Architected Framework, and how does it appear on the exam?

back.answer: AWS's definition of what good looks like in the cloud; on the exam it is a lens on questions, not its own question.
back.explanation: Six pillars act as the checks. They appear as qualifiers in questions rather than as 'which pillar' questions.
back.mnemonic: A building inspector's checklist: a house can stand and still fail inspection.

cards.front: Well-Architected Framework: how many pillars, and what are they?

back.answer: Six: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
back.explanation: Walkthrough: how you run it, lock it, how it survives, how fast it goes, what it costs, what it burns.
back.mnemonic: Operations Secure Reliable Performance Costs Sustainably.

cards.front: Well-Architected Operational Excellence pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Run and improve: everything as code, small reversible changes. CloudFormation, CloudWatch.
back.explanation: Use infrastructure as code, deploy frequently in small rollback-able steps, and learn from every failure.

cards.front: Well-Architected Security pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Least privilege, defense in depth, encrypt everywhere. IAM, KMS, GuardDuty.
back.explanation: Grant only what's needed, defend in layers (WAF + security groups + NACLs), encrypt at rest and in transit.

cards.front: Well-Architected Reliability pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Survive failures, recover automatically, stop guessing capacity. Multi-AZ, Auto Scaling Groups, Route 53.
back.explanation: Assume everything fails and design so nobody notices: Multi-AZ, health checks, auto-recovery.

cards.front: Well-Architected Performance Efficiency pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Right tool for the job, serverless-first, go global. Lambda, CloudFront, ElastiCache.
back.explanation: Don't run a database on EC2 when RDS exists; cache with CloudFront/ElastiCache; experiment often.

cards.front: Well-Architected Cost Optimization pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Pay only for what you use, and measure it. Cost Explorer, Savings Plans, Spot.
back.explanation: Right-size, use Spot for interruptible work, Savings Plans for steady work, and look at the bill.

cards.front: Well-Architected Sustainability pillar: essence and flagship services?

back.answer: Maximize utilization, minimize wasted compute. Graviton, serverless.
back.explanation: The newest pillar: fewer idle servers, efficient hardware, serverless where possible.

cards.front: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?

back.answer: A free console questionnaire; you answer per pillar about a workload and it produces an improvement plan.
back.explanation: Cue: 'review our architecture against best practices at no cost'.

cards.front: In Well-Architected exam questions, where do the pillars usually hide?

back.answer: In the qualifier: 'MOST cost-effective', 'improve reliability', 'LEAST operational overhead'.
back.explanation: Typically two answers would work; the pillar keyword tells you which one AWS wants.

cards.sourceHeading: The exam angle (this is the real payoff)

cards.front: Well-Architected exam trap when two options both solve the problem?

back.answer: Answering the working solution instead of the qualified one; the capitalized adjective picks the winner.
back.explanation: Read the qualifier first, not last.

cards.sourceHeading: The exam angle (this is the real payoff)

cards.front: Two solutions both meet requirements; the question asks for the MOST cost-effective. Fault-tolerant batch workload. Which?

back.answer: The cheaper one that still works, e.g. Spot over On-Demand.

cards.front: Improve reliability of a single-AZ RDS database. What do you do?

back.answer: Enable Multi-AZ.
back.explanation: Reliability pillar: survive AZ failure with automatic failover.

cards.front: LEAST operational overhead to run containers. Which choice?

back.answer: Fargate over the EC2 launch type.

cards.front: Improve performance for global users. Which service?

back.answer: CloudFront.
back.explanation: Performance Efficiency: go global, cache at the edge.

cards.front: Ensure the architecture follows AWS best practices at no additional cost. Which?

back.answer: AWS Well-Architected Tool.
back.explanation: A free console questionnaire that yields an improvement plan.

cards.front: Reduce the environmental impact of the workload. Which approach?

back.answer: Graviton instances / serverless.

cards.front: Keyword: **"IaC, small reversible changes"**

back.answer: Operational Excellence (CloudFormation)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Least privilege, encrypt everywhere"**

back.answer: Security (IAM, KMS, GuardDuty)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Survive failure, stop guessing capacity"**

back.answer: Reliability (Multi-AZ, ASG, Route 53)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Right tool, serverless-first, edge"**

back.answer: Performance Efficiency (Lambda, CloudFront)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Pay for what you use, measure spend"**

back.answer: Cost Optimization (Cost Explorer, Savings Plans, Spot)

cards.front: Keyword: **"Maximize utilization, Graviton"**

back.answer: Sustainability

cards.front: Keyword: **"Free best-practices review"**

back.answer: Well-Architected Tool

cards.front: Keyword: **"MOST cost-effective / LEAST overhead"**

back.answer: The qualifier picks between two working answers
